findings.description: Direct inspection of all five V196 main views and six pose renders shows the overskirt remains covered in dense, sharp triangular fragments and folds instead of reading as a coherent sewn pleated surface. The lower self-collision distance materially reduced, but did not resolve, the visible breakup. The V196 native cloth geometry audit still records 2,967 inverted skirt source-fan triangles of 20,701 (14.3%); this is prototype instability evidence, not acceptance.

Direct V196 crouch and sit renders show the lap pulled away/fragmented, with substantial anterior thigh exposure; the side views show long detached-looking strips extending from the hem. The pose diagnostic independently reports only 31.4–39.8% sampled overskirt coverage on each upper thigh and 21.9–25.9% front-lap ray coverage in these poses. These geometric samples are diagnostics, not fit or visual acceptance.
The V196 front, side, and three-quarter renders still show angular, faceted jacket surface artifacts around the torso and an uneven waist transition.

nextAction: Keep V196 rejected. Its schema-bound 3 mm native self-collision setting reduced inverted skirt fan triangles from V195 7,447/20,701 to V196 2,967/20,701 and reduced front-lap maximum displacement from 122.2/125.8 mm to 89.7/84.1 mm, but direct V196 renders remain visibly broken and pose coverage remains poor. For one controlled next prototype, disable overskirt self-collision while retaining native body collision and all panel, bending, pin, weight, and other solver settings. Bind the changed value to this same overskirt component and measure fresh geometry and poses; retain rejection unless direct views become coherent and usable.
